title: Design Video Streaming (YouTube / Netflix)
relevance: High — canonical 45-min HLD at FAANG + Indian product cos (Meta, Google, Amazon, Netflix, Uber, Flipkart); tests blob upload, async pipelines, CDN, and ABR more than novel algorithms.
company_notes: Campus/new-grad: very common “design YouTube” covering upload + CDN + multi-quality; ABR/DAG depth differentiates. Experienced/FAANG (1–5+ YOE): same prompt with probes on multipart resume, transcoding parallelism, CDN tiers, hot-video, cost; Netflix loops lean Open Connect + control vs data plane. Top-tier canonical HLD alongside URL shortener, chat, and news feed.

phases.goal: Scope VOD upload+watch in/out, non-functionals, and YouTube-UGC vs Netflix-catalog shape.

must_hit.point: Functional in-scope: upload video, stream/watch with start in ~2–3s, and resumable upload.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists upload, low-latency first play (~2–3s), and resumable upload as the core product loop.

must_hit.point: Park comments, search, recommendations, live, DRM, and moderation unless the interviewer asks.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explicitly marks those as out / below-the-line and confirms with interviewer.

must_hit.point: Non-functionals: high availability, global low-latency playback, multi-device / variable bandwidth; scale framing ~1M uploads/day and ~100M watches/day (or own numbers stuck to).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States HA, global latency, ABR-friendly clients, and cites the Hello Interview scale numbers or commits to alternatives.

must_hit.point: Clarify YouTube-like UGC vs Netflix-like catalog because it changes CDN fill strategy.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Asks UGC+long-tail pull CDN vs finite catalog proactive fill before drawing architecture.

probes: Is this YouTube-style UGC or Netflix-style catalog, and what is explicitly out of scope for this 45-min design?

hints.1: Start by locking upload + watch, then ask what to cut.
hints.2: Separate functional in/out from NFRs and UGC vs catalog.
hints.3: In: upload, ~2–3s start, resumable; out: comments/search/recs/live/DRM/moderation; note catalog shape drives CDN fill.

phases.goal: Show upload rate, storage multiplier, watch starts, and why egress—not API QPS—forces a CDN.

must_hit.point: Uploads: 1M/day ≈ 12/sec average with peak 10×; avg raw size ~100–500 MB → tens of PB/year raw before encoding.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Walks 1M/day → ~12/sec, peak 10×, and ~100–500 MB driving tens of PB/year raw.

must_hit.point: Storage multiplies because each title becomes many renditions × segments (often 5–10×+ raw depending on ladder).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Calls out ladder/segment blow-up as 5–10×+ raw, not one blob per title.

must_hit.point: Watch side: 100M watches/day ≈ ~1k starts/sec avg; concurrent viewers and bitrate (e.g. 3–5 Mbps) drive egress Tbps—hence CDN.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Converts watches to ~1k starts/sec and pivots to Tbps egress from 3–5 Mbps, not API QPS.

must_hit.point: Transcode CPU is the write-path bottleneck; size the worker pool from upload rate × encode-minutes-per-video.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sizes encode fleet from upload rate times encode-minutes, not from playback QPS.

probes: Walk the back-of-envelope from 1M uploads/day and 100M watches/day—what dominates cost and capacity?

hints.1: Estimate write path and read path separately.
hints.2: Uploads → storage+encode; watches → starts/sec and egress Tbps.
hints.3: 1M/day≈12/sec (peak 10×), ~100–500 MB and 5–10×+ storage; 100M watches≈~1k starts/sec; 3–5 Mbps → egress Tbps → CDN.

phases.goal: Define control-plane APIs for metadata/presign/complete while playback hits CDN directly.

must_hit.point: POST /videos creates metadata in processing and returns videoId plus presigned multipart upload URLs (or POST /videos/{id}/upload-urls).
must_hit.evidence_hint: API issues presigned multipart URLs and stores metadata; client does not upload video bytes through the API.

must_hit.point: POST /videos/{id}/complete finalizes multipart and enqueues transcode; optional PATCH /videos/{id}/parts tracks resume state.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Complete triggers enqueue; parts endpoint (or equivalent) supports resumable multipart state.

must_hit.point: GET /videos/{id} returns metadata, status (processing|ready), and manifest URL on the CDN; player fetches manifest/segments from CDN, not the API.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States status + CDN manifest URL and that segment GETs bypass app servers.

must_hit.point: Optional POST /videos/{id}/views is async for view counting if in scope.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions async view posting as optional, not on the playback hot path.

probes: What does the client call to upload a large video and then start playback?

hints.1: API is control plane; media bytes take another path.
hints.2: Create → presign multipart → complete/enqueue → GET metadata+manifest.
hints.3: POST /videos (+ upload-urls), optional parts PATCH, POST complete, GET ready+CDN manifest; player GETs CDN objects.

phases.goal: Separate metadata/status from blob keys and optional resume/rendition records.

must_hit.point: Video(video_id PK, uploader_id, title, description, status, duration_s, created_at, primary_manifest_url, thumbnail_url) with point lookups by videoId.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows a Video row keyed by video_id including status and primary_manifest_url.

must_hit.point: Blobs in object storage with keys like raw/{video_id}/…, encoded/{video_id}/{rendition}/seg_00001.ts, manifests/{video_id}/master.m3u8; metadata in DB (+ Redis), not in API memory.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates DB metadata from S3/GCS key layout for raw, segments, and manifests.

must_hit.point: UploadPart(video_id, part_no, etag, status) for multipart resume; optional VideoRendition(video_id, codec, resolution, bitrate_kbps, media_manifest_url) or fold into manifests only.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Tracks part etag/status for resume and either stores renditions or relies on manifests.

must_hit.point: Metadata store choices: Cassandra/Dynamo partitioned by video_id or Postgres + cache; view counters as a separate write-heavy store / Redis buffer if in scope.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Picks a video_id-partitioned metadata store and isolates hot counters if views are in scope.

probes: Where do status, manifests, segment objects, and resume state live?

hints.1: Split metadata rows from blob keys.
hints.2: Video row + object key prefixes; add UploadPart if resume is required.
hints.3: Video with primary_manifest_url/status; raw/encoded/manifests keys; UploadPart etags; optional VideoRendition or manifest-only.

phases.goal: Draw two planes: async upload/transcode write path and CDN-served playback read path.

must_hit.point: Never push video bytes through API servers on the hot path: client → API/LB for auth/metadata/presign → Metadata DB + Redis; raw object storage via direct multipart upload.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Clearly separates control-plane API from direct-to-object-storage uploads.

must_hit.point: Queue → transcode workers (DAG: split → parallel encode bitrate ladder → package HLS/DASH → manifests) → encoded object storage → mark metadata ready.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes queue-orchestrated DAG ending in manifests and status ready.

must_hit.point: Playback: CDN (edge → optional regional/origin shield) serves segments; origin is the encoded bucket; player is latency-critical and read-heavy.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows player→CDN→origin shield→encoded bucket as the streaming path.

must_hit.point: YouTube-shaped default is UGC + long-tail + pull CDN; contrast Netflix Open Connect proactive fill to ISP appliances for a finite catalog.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Starts YouTube-shaped then contrasts Open Connect fill for Netflix-like catalogs.

probes: Sketch the upload flow and the streaming flow as two diagrams—what components sit on each?

hints.1: Two planes: write-heavy async vs read-heavy sync.
hints.2: Presign to object store; queue+DAG encode; CDN for playback.
hints.3: Client→API/presign→raw bucket; queue→FFmpeg DAG→encoded+manifests→ready; player→CDN/edge (shield)→origin bucket; note pull CDN vs Open Connect.

phases.goal: Defend ABR packaging, parallel encode, CDN ownership, encode eagerness, and view-count consistency choices.

must_hit.point: ABR vs single file: ~2–10s segments + ladder enable mid-play quality switches and CDN caching; costs more storage/CPU for smoother UX on flaky networks. Server serves immutable HTTP objects while the client switches on throughput/buffer health.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explains manifests/segments, client-driven ABR, and immutable CDN objects vs one progressive file.

must_hit.point: DAG parallel encode vs sequential: wall-clock minutes vs hours; needs orchestrator, idempotent workers, and temp storage by URL.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Argues parallel bitrate/segment encode with idempotent workers over a single long encode.

must_hit.point: Commercial CDN vs own Open Connect: buy until egress economics/ISP partnerships justify building; Netflix pre-positions catalog, YouTube pull-caches long tail.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Ties CDN build-vs-buy to egress and contrasts proactive fill vs pull caching.

must_hit.point: Eager vs lazy encode: full ladder on upload (fast first play) vs popular-formats-first / on-demand rare rungs (save cost, slower long-tail quality).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States when to encode full ladder immediately versus defer rare rungs.

probes: Why segment into an ABR ladder instead of one file, and when would you build your own CDN?

hints.1: Pick two tradeoffs: packaging and encode/CDN cost.
hints.2: ABR segments + parallel DAG; then CDN buy-vs-build / eager-vs-lazy.
hints.3: ~2–10s segments + client ABR; parallel idempotent DAG; buy CDN until Open Connect economics; eager full ladder vs popular-first.

phases.goal: Scale egress/origin, transcode backlog, hot metadata, upload failures, and geo latency.

must_hit.point: Viral egress/origin melt: target 95%+ segment traffic at edge; use origin shield / tiered cache, and pre-warm first segments of hot titles.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites 95%+ edge hit ratio, origin shield, and pre-warm of first segments for hot videos.

must_hit.point: Transcode backlog: autoscale workers, priority queues (creators/trending), degrade ladder under load.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Scales encode fleet and sheds rare rungs / reorders queue under backlog.

must_hit.point: Metadata hot key: Redis cache, replicate popular rows, avoid single-partition overload; uploads use multipart resume, idempotent complete, and TTL GC for incomplete objects.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Caches/replicates hot video metadata and hardens multipart complete + incomplete-object GC.

must_hit.point: Geo latency: multi-region metadata + edge CDN; object-storage cross-region replication is for DR, not for every playback hop.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Puts playback locality on CDN/edge and treats CRR as DR, not the primary watch path.

probes: A video goes viral—what melts first and how do you protect origin and transcode?

hints.1: Think edge hit ratio before adding API capacity.
hints.2: CDN/shield/pre-warm for reads; autoscale/priority/degrade for encode.
hints.3: 95%+ edge + origin shield + pre-warm; worker autoscaling and ladder degrade; Redis for hot metadata; multipart resume + TTL GC; CDN for geo, CRR for DR.

tradeoffs.topic: ABR segments + ladder vs single file
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Segments (~2–10s) and a bitrate ladder let the client switch quality mid-play from throughput/buffer health and make immutable objects CDN-cacheable; you pay more storage/CPU versus one progressive file that fails on flaky networks.

tradeoffs.topic: DAG parallel encode vs sequential encode
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Parallel split→encode→package cuts wall-clock from hours toward minutes but needs a queue orchestrator, idempotent workers, and temp object URLs; sequential is simpler and much slower.

tradeoffs.topic: Commercial CDN vs Netflix Open Connect
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Buy a pull CDN until egress cost and ISP partnerships justify building; Netflix pre-positions a finite catalog on ISP appliances, while YouTube-style UGC relies on pull caching for a long tail.

tradeoffs.topic: Eager full ladder vs lazy / popular-first encode
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Encoding the full ladder on upload maximizes fast first play everywhere; encoding popular formats first and rare rungs on demand saves cost at the expense of slower long-tail quality.
Redis INCR with periodic flush (or CQRS) trades stricter consistency for lower write amplification on a write-heavy counter path.

gotchas.trap: Treating live streaming like VOD batch transcode.
gotchas.correction: Live needs low-latency real-time ingest, shorter segments, and different packaging—do not pretend the batch DAG is live.

gotchas.trap: Streaming video bytes through app servers.
gotchas.correction: API stays control plane (auth, metadata, presign); pushing media through app servers blows bandwidth and cost—player reads from CDN.

gotchas.trap: Ignoring auth differences for paid vs public content.
gotchas.correction: Netflix-like paid content needs DRM / signed URLs / token auth; public UGC often uses softer CDN-cached controls.

gotchas.trap: Forgetting processing UX and cold-start origin spikes.
gotchas.correction: Generate thumbnails/previews and show processing while encode runs; empty edge cache after publish causes origin spikes—pre-push or origin shield.
Codec is compression (e.g. H.264); HLS/DASH is packaging/protocol for HTTP segment delivery.

gotchas.trap: Dragging recommendations/search into the core design.
gotchas.correction: They are separate systems—acknowledge and park unless the interviewer pulls you there.
